questions.question:
Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Full of hot air

options.text: From all parts of the world

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- **'​Full of nonsense'** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom **'****Full of hot air****'** is 'Full of nonsense'.
 
• Let’s look at the meaning and example of the given phrasal verb:
 
 
• Full of hot air- "Full of lies, exaggerations, or nonsense." (झूठ, अतिशयोक्ति या बकवास से भरा हुआ।)
 
 
• *E.g. Not one bit of snow at all—those meteorologists are **full of hot air.***
 
 
 
 
 
• *​​*Thus from the explanation given above, we find that the 3rd option is the correct choice.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in bold.

All this puts the party on the ground __**in the shade**__.

options.text: To be inferior to someone or something
Under the shade of a tree

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'To be inferior to someone or something'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• The meaning of the given phrase is **"in a state or position of inferiority, inadequacy, or unimportance relative to something else".**
 
• We use the phrase to refer to a state or position in which one person is less important than another.
 
 
• **Example:** As always, my good grades were put** in the shade **by my brother's football achievements.
 
 
 
• Hence, **option 2** is the correct answer.

options.text: ended one's association with someone or something
changed the parts and machinery of something

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **ended one's association with someone or something**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The idiom '**washed my hands of__**' means to refuse to accept responsibility for; abandon or renounce (**जिम्मेदारी स्वीकार करने से इनकार; छोड़ देना या त्यागना**)

 __
 
• ​Example: She seems to **have washed her hands of** the job.​
 
 
 
• The sentence implies that the subject__** __I __**__got rid of the car long ago__.

 

*Therefore, the correct answer is option 2)*

• An idiom is an expression whose meaning is different from the meanings of the individual words in it.

 
 
• Ex: *'**To bring something home to somebody’ means ‘To make somebody understand something'*

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.
